title: Budgets Shape Geometry; States Compress History
subtitle: BMuon · Small-scale extrapolation · Async RL · Linear Transformers
intro: Channel budgets, small-model extrapolation, and gradient bias from stale rollouts: seven newly collected research items and technical articles, plus two version records whose substantive changes remain unverified. Original dates are retained; none is presented as first published today. The classic asks how linear attention compresses a growing history into a fixed-size state.

articles.paper: PONDER: Learning to Generate in the Right Order
articles.authors: Julius Erbach · Dominik Narnhofer · Bernt Schiele · Jan Eric Lenssen · Konrad Schindler
articles.title: PONDER: spend extra compute on which positions to revise
articles.evidence: Read Section 3.3, Section 4, and Appendices A.3–A.4

blocks.text: Freeze the generator and train a fill/remove position policy. N empty positions and R removals require N+2R position decisions, not that many backbone calls. For a fixed Sudoku policy trained at R=9, hard accuracy rises from 56.60% at R=0 to 96.68% at R=9 and 98.61% at R=128; evaluation uses 30,000 held-out boards balanced across three difficulty levels. This is not a compute-matched comparison.[4]

articles.paper: Bridging Compressed Communication and Local Steps via Spectral Method in Federated Learning
articles.authors: Dmitriy Bystrov · George Chirkov · Daniil Medyakov · Dmitry Bylinkin · Aleksandr Beznosikov
articles.title: Federated Muon: combine local steps with communication compression

blocks.text: The authors propose a spectral method supporting both local updates and compression, and report convergence without bounded heterogeneity. Full assumptions, compressor details, and communication-round bounds have not been checked; no claim is made for arbitrary client distributions.[5]

articles.paper: Learning to Discriminate Scene Structures Makes Self-Supervised Depth Learning Scalable
articles.authors: Mengtan Zhang · Yuchuan Cui · Yu Ma · Zizhan Guo · Wei Ye · Rui Fan
articles.title: MaSS: why mixed-domain data can hurt depth estimation

blocks.text: Separating scene structure from context targets conflicts in mixed-domain training. The authors report separate/joint training on 4 domains and zero-shot evaluation on 8 others. Included under data mixing, not as evidence of a universal fitted power law; matched sample budgets remain unchecked.[6]

classic.title: Linear Transformers: turning history into state
classic.dateNote: First posted June 29, 2020; read the ICML 2020 / PMLR 119 proceedings version
classic.evidence: Read Sections 3.1–3.4, Algorithm 1, and Section 4.2.1; checked the equation page and Table 1

recognition.label: ICML 2020 · Foundational work in linear attention

classic.question: If two distinct histories produce identical (Sₜ,zₜ) but the next query requires different answers, this layer cannot distinguish them. Can we construct a minimal collision and identify what additional state is needed?

blocks.text: The Transformer (2017) lets each query retrieve the entire history, with a growing cache. This ICML 2020 work uses finite-dimensional kernel features to compress history into a matrix state: it changes the attention kernel rather than obtaining exact softmax at no cost.[10,11]

blocks.label: q and k are queries/keys, v∈ℝᵈᵛ; positive features ensure a positive denominator. This is the experimental kernel

blocks.tex: S_t=\sum_{j\le t}\phi(k_j)v_j^\top\in\mathbb R^{m\times d_v},\quad z_t=\sum_{j\le t}\phi(k_j),\qquad y_t=\frac{S_t^\top\phi(q_t)}{z_t^\top\phi(q_t)}
blocks.label: Equations (9)–(12), rewritten in column-vector notation: aggregate KV before answering queries
S₀=z₀=0; at fixed feature dimensions, inference state is independent of sequence length (excluding projections and other layers)

blocks.title: Evidence boundary
blocks.text: A finite-m ELU kernel is not the exponential softmax kernel. Fixed state saves computation while compressing history into the same statistics; these identities do not guarantee lossless arbitrary long-range retrieval.

blocks.title: Discussion question
blocks.text: If two distinct histories produce identical (Sₜ,zₜ) but the next query requires different answers, this layer cannot distinguish them. Can we construct a minimal collision and identify what additional state is needed?
